australianrent

https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-xzha0419/

This package aims to help tenants answer the question: “Which local government area can I really afford to rent in?” Rental affordability is personal. Published median rents are the same for all readers, but whether those rents are affordable differs between households with incomes of $900 and $2,500. The package therefore includes not only published rental data but also a function that checks all areas against a user-specified income. It also includes a Shiny app that visualizes the results and allows users to compare rental prices in any three LGAs over time.

Data

vic_rents includes quarterly median advertised rents from June 1999 to September 2025 by property type. The data has 58,618 rows covering 79 local government areas, 7 property types and 106 quarters.

Cautions - Median number only include the newly signed leases but not the whole market. - Homes Victoria will replace the median price to NA if this quarter has too few lettings.

Source: Homes Victoria, Rental Report — Quarterly: Quarterly Median Rents by LGA, September quarter 2025, published on data.gov.au under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australia licence.

The script that downloads and reshapes the source workbook is in data-raw/vic-rents.R.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

#need to install "remotes" package first
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-xzha0419")

Launching the app 

library(australianrent)
run_app()

The app reads the data installed with the package, so internet connection and external files are not needed.

Example

Search the areas where the median rent for a one-bedroom flat is within 40% of a gross weekly household income of $1000.

library(australianrent)

result <- rent_affordability(
  weekly_income = 1000,
  property_type = "1 bedroom flat",
  threshold = 0.40
)

head(result)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   region            lga          quarter    Median Count income_share affordable
#>   <chr>             <chr>        <date>      <dbl> <dbl>        <dbl> <lgl>     
#> 1 Barwon South West Colac-Otway  2025-09-01    290     9         0.29 TRUE      
#> 2 Barwon South West Corangamite  2025-09-01     NA    NA        NA    NA        
#> 3 Barwon South West Glenelg      2025-09-01    300     5         0.3  TRUE      
#> 4 Barwon South West Greater Gee… 2025-09-01    340   140         0.34 TRUE      
#> 5 Barwon South West Moyne        2025-09-01     NA    NA        NA    NA        
#> 6 Barwon South West Queenscliffe 2025-09-01     NA    NA        NA    NA

The weekly rental budget is $400.

  • Median is the median weekly rent in Australian dollars.

  • income_share is the proportion of household income spent on rent.

  • affordable is TRUE when the median rent is within the budget.

  • NA indicates unavailable data.

What’s in the package

Component Purpose
vic_rents Quarterly median rents by local government area, 1999 to 2025
rent_affordability() Compare every area’s median rent against a given income
run_app() Launch the Shiny app

Generative AI declaration

ChatGPT and Shiny Assistant have been used in this package to understand the unfamiliar code, to structure the approach to the data preparation and package layout, to learn how Shiny works (particularly reactive expressions and input validation), to debug errors and check whether the package ran correctly. All output by AI has been reviewed by myself before publish.
